subject: Outage budget and latency split — exception request for monthly credits
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmereal.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmereal.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA ask — outage budget + monthly credit cap and latency split

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. AcmeReal is close to committing, but procurement has pushed back on the standard SLA language. Two asks from our side:

1) Monthly "outage budget" — for our seasonal spikes we need some flexibility so we don't breach credits for short burst incidents. We want an explicit monthly outage budget (e.g., up to X minutes per month) before credits apply, and a higher per-month credit cap (current template seems too punitive for our pattern).

2) Latency SLO split — we run mixed workloads (interactive UI calls ~95th percentile and background batch scoring). We need the SLA to separate interactive (p95) and batch (p99), because the current single-latency SLO doesn't map to our operations.

Can Redwood provide an exception to the standard uptime % / credit cap for a committed customer tier? If so, what is the formal request process and timeline? We can share request data and a week of traffic samples if that helps.

Attached are our current procurement notes. Hoping we can get a counterproposal this week — need to review with legal.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Director, Platform Ops
AcmeReal
[Attachment: acmereal_procurement_notes.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmereal.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — outage budget + monthly credit cap and latency split

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear summary and the notes.

Short answer: we can offer an exception path for committed customers but we need alignment across Sales, Legal, and Product on the exact mechanics. Proposed next steps:

- Sales (Ben) to propose a revised monthly credit cap and outage budget band that maps to your monthly volume profile.
- Product/Engineering to define the latency tier split and what metrics (p95/p99) we'll measure in the SLA.
- Legal (Marcus) to draft a short amendment/redline to the standard SLA (one-pager) showing the carveout and credit calculation.

I've attached a baseline redline template and a small downtime logging CSV we ask customers to use for any operational post-mortem. Ben/Marcus — can you take the lead on numbers and legal language? Sanjay, if you can send a week of representative traffic (timestamps + request types) to ops@acmereal.com we will baseline the outage budget.

I'm keeping the scope limited: aim for an amendment that changes only the monthly credit cap and adds an appendix with latency buckets — no wholesale SLA rewrite. If all OK, we can aim for a signed amendment within ~10 business days.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_sla_redline.pdf (pdf, 234KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmereal.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — outage budget + monthly credit cap and latency split

Sanjay — looping in Laura from Product to confirm latency measurement approach. Preliminary proposal from Sales:

- Outage budget: allow a rolling 45-minute monthly outage budget for AcmeReal's production pool before credits are triggered. This is intended to absorb short maintenance or transient infra blips.
- Monthly credit cap: increase cap to 15% of monthly service fees (from standard 10%) for your committed tier.
- Latency split proposal: interactive calls measured at p95 with a target of 250ms; batch scoring measured at p99 with a target of 1.5s. Credits tied to percent below target on a per-bucket basis.

Laura — can you confirm we can instrument and report p95/p99 per route and that the interactive/batch split is feasible? Also, we should document how maintenance windows count against the outage budget.

If these numbers look reasonable to you (Sanjay), I will ask Marcus to prepare the amendment draft.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmereal.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — outage budget + monthly credit cap and latency split

Ben / Sanjay — product/engineering confirmation below:

- We can report per-route p95 and p99 with our existing telemetry. We'll need you to map which endpoints are "interactive" vs "batch" — a short list is fine.
- Maintenance windows: planned maintenance that you approve in advance and that we post to the status page will be excluded from the outage budget. Unplanned incidents count toward the budget.
- Measurement: we'll use 30-day rolling windows for monthly calculations, and report credits on the following invoice cycle.

One caveat: the 45-minute outage budget is workable, but for sustained distributed incidents (partial region degradation) our incident classification will need to be explicit in the amendment so both sides agree on what counts as a single outage vs multiple events. I'll add a brief definition section in the redline.

I'll attach a short mapping template for your endpoints.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Product Lead, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: endpoint_latency_mapping_template.csv (csv, 2KB)]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmereal.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — outage budget + monthly credit cap and latency split

Sanjay / team — I reviewed the numbers and drafted a one-page amendment. Key legal/ops points included in the redline:

- Definitions: explicit "Outage Budget" definition (rolling monthly minutes) and how overlapping incidents are aggregated.
- Credit calculation: step function tied to monthly availability bands with the elevated 15% cap; credits will be applied as service credits only, not cash refunds.
- Maintenance carveout: approved planned maintenance windows and security patches (with 48-hour notice) excluded.
- Latency buckets: define routes and measurement (p95 for interactive; p99 for batch).
- Audit: Redwood will provide monthly measurement reports; AcmeReal can request a one-time audit per year if metrics are in dispute (reasonable costs may apply).

I've attached the redline (see 'proposed_sla_redline.pdf' in the thread). Once Sanjay confirms the endpoint mapping, we'll populate the appendix and circulate the final DocuSign link for signatures.

Marcus Lin
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: downtime_logging_template.csv (csv, 1KB)]
